correctness.rationale: With J^3=0 and dim J/J²=2, dim J²=1, multiplication is exactly nonzero symmetric B:V×V->kz, and every automorphism acts by (r,v,s)->(r,gv,tau(v)+c s) where B(gv,gw)=c B(v,w), tau in V*. On v≠0 unrestricted tau makes a q-fold orbit over each similitude orbit in V, while on v=0 the multiplier subgroup controls k*z. Rank-one B yields two V orbits and square-class socle split in odd characteristic; odd rank-two split forms have isotropic/off-conic orbits, anisotropic norms transitive; even alternating forms have GL2 transitivity and even nonalternating forms preserve the isotropic line with explicit shear transitivity. Each predicted row sums to q³ in each fixed residue fiber. Independently exhaustive enumeration of every nonzero symmetric form and its exact similitude orbits for F2 (7 forms), F3 (26 forms) and F5 (124 forms) reproduces full orbit multisets; the supplied checker covers F4 (63 forms) additionally. The infinite q theorem rests on group-theoretic form classification, not finite tests alone.

value.rationale: PASS: Complete orbit-size data of the intrinsic automorphism action on elements is a natural invariant for a specified full finite-field Hilbert stratum, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It detects various multiplication forms while also exhibiting a meaningful failure of detection: in characteristic two, nonisomorphic rank-one non-Gorenstein and nonsingular nonalternating Gorenstein algebras share an identical element-orbit-size multiset. The exact all-prime-power phase classification is reusable for equivariant counting and symmetry analysis.
